issues.problem: noteTH says the past forms are 'rang and rung'; rung is the past participle, not the past simple, so learners may write 'I rung you'.

fix.noteTH: ใช้มากในอังกฤษ ส่วน call ใช้ได้ทั่วไป กริยาผิดปกติ: ring – rang – rung

issues.problem: gapOk too optimistic: 'Can you suggest a good place to eat near here?' is equally correct and very common.
gapOk too optimistic: 'cut' or 'lowered' fit the gap equally well ('cut the price by half').
gapOk too optimistic: after 'First,' the answer 'Second,' is equally correct (also 'Also').
gapOk too optimistic: 'Unfortunately,' fits the gap equally well.
gapOk too optimistic: 'lately' fits 'Have you seen any good films ___?' equally well.
gapOk too optimistic: 'A newspaper journalist wrote a story...' is equally correct.
exampleTH 'ตอนลดราคาครึ่งราคา' is redundant/awkward Thai.

fix.exampleTH: ฉันซื้อกางเกงยีนส์ตัวนี้ตอนร้านจัดลดราคา ได้มาในราคาครึ่งเดียว

issues.problem: Collocation 'rather than' belongs to a different sense (instead of), not 'quite'.
Collocation 'hard as rock' is not idiomatic (it is 'as hard as a rock' / 'rock-hard').
noteTH is ambiguous: reads as if only trash/garbage are uncountable; rubbish is uncountable too.

fix.noteTH: เป็นคำนามนับไม่ได้ ใช้ในอังกฤษ ส่วนอเมริกันใช้ trash หรือ garbage
